messages.content: i want to tell my family about a walk i took. please keep it simple, like something i would say at dinner.
tell me a few things that happened on the walk, and i can help put them into a short story.
i left after lunch. i went past the library, saw a friend near the market, and got home before the rain.
i went for a walk after lunch. i walked past the library and saw a friend near the market. i got home before the rain started.
can you make it sound less like a list?
after lunch, i went for a walk past the library. near the market, i saw a friend. i got home before the rain started, so i was inside when the weather changed.
what if the rain did not start until hours later?
then the rain may not have been important to how you felt about getting home. you can say i got home before the rain without making it sound like the rain began right after you came inside.
keep only what i gave, but make the order easy to follow.
after lunch, i walked past the library and saw a friend near the market. i was home before the rain.
can you add how i felt?
only if you tell me, or if you want a made up feeling for a story. you have not said how the walk felt to you.
i felt calm. put that in the last sentence.
after lunch, i walked past the library and saw a friend near the market. i felt calm when i got home, before the rain.
is my mother and my father is home correct?
use my mother and my father are home. you are talking about two people together, so are is correct there.
what if only my mother is home?
then say my mother is home. that sentence is about one person.
can i say my family is home?
yes. my family is home is a useful sentence when you are talking about the family as one group.
does that mean i can know every person in the family is there?
not always. people may use family in a general way. if it is important that every person is there, say everyone in my family is home.
what if i know only my parents are there?
then say my parents are home. that gives the group you know about without adding other people.
now ask whether my parents are home.
are my parents home?
answer if only my father is there.
my father is home, but my mother is not.
why is that better than just yes?
because yes could make it sound like both parents are home. saying who is there gives the real information.
write a story about a person hearing a radio from another room and thinking someone is home. the radio should not be enough to know for sure.

a woman came into the house and heard a voice in the kitchen. she thought her brother was talking on the phone, so she called hello and waited. nobody answered. when she looked into the kitchen, she saw the radio on the table. the voice was coming from it. her brother had left the radio on before going to the market. she turned it down and looked for his message. he had written that he would be back after buying food. she had heard a real voice, but that had not told her for sure that a person was in the room.
what made her think someone was there?
she heard a voice from the kitchen and thought it was her brother.
was hearing the voice false?
no. the sound was real. her first idea about where it came from was wrong.
why is that difference useful?
it helps keep what she heard and what she thought apart. a real sound can still lead to an idea that needs more information.
use words from the story to explain.
she heard talking. she did not yet know that the talking came from the radio instead of her brother.
what could she say when her brother comes home?
i thought you were home because i heard the radio. then i found your message.
can she say she saw him in the kitchen?
no. she heard a voice, but did not see him. that would change the story.
finish with her reading his message before choosing where to look next.
she read that he had gone to the market and would return soon. she left the kitchen and put her things away while waiting.
my list says bread, cheese, and rice. can you know that i do not need milk?
no. the list gives three things you wrote down. it does not say whether it is the whole list or whether you already have milk.
now i say this is the whole list of what i need to buy today.
then milk is not on the list of what you need to buy today. that still does not tell us whether there is milk at home or whether you use it.
why not say i never drink milk?
not having to buy milk today is different from never drinking it. your list is about a task for today, not every part of your life.
what if i add milk now?
then your list has bread, cheese, rice, and milk. adding milk changes what you plan to buy today.
say how many things are on the list now.
there are four things on the list: bread, cheese, rice, and milk.
if i take cheese off the list, how many things are left?
three things are left: bread, rice, and milk.
can you know which one i will buy first?
no. the order of words on the list does not tell us your order at the shop unless you say it does.
my friend asked me to go to the library with them today. i like that they asked, but i cannot go. help me say both.
thank you for asking me. i cannot come today, but it was nice to hear from you.
please put my answer for today before the words about hearing from them.
thank you for asking me. i cannot come today, but i liked hearing from you.
can i say i hope they have a good time?
yes. that gives a kind wish without making a plan for yourself.
write all of that together.
thank you for asking me. i cannot come today, but i hope you have a good time at the library.
why did you leave out liked hearing from you?
you wanted a thank you, a clear answer for today, and a kind wish. those three parts already make a full reply. i can put that feeling back if you want it too.
put it back, but keep the whole thing short.
thanks for asking. it was nice to hear from you. i cannot come today, but i hope you enjoy the library.
what if they ask why i cannot come?
you can give the real reason if you want, or say that you have another plan. do not make up a reason just to make the answer sound better.
i am at home and my sister is at the shop. should i ask when she is coming home or going home?
when are you coming home is a good choice when you are at home and asking when she will come there. going home can also be understood, but coming is useful for talking about the place where you are.
what if i am at the shop with her and we are talking about leaving?
then you can ask when are we going home? you are both away from home and talking about going there.
can return home work too?
yes. return home says someone goes back home after being away. it can be useful if you want to talk about going back without choosing between come and go.
make that explanation shorter.
return home is about going back home. it does not need to make the same choice between come and go.
now write a short question to my sister while i wait at home.
when are you coming home?
can you know she lives with me from the first message?
not for sure. home could be a place you share, but you have not given that detail clearly.
we do share the house. now ask if she wants dinner when she gets back.
would you like dinner when you get home?
why not say dinner is already cooked?
because you have not said it is cooked. the question can ask what she wants without adding that fact.
write a story about a child learning a new word and asking for one example rather than a long explanation.

a child asked her teacher what before could mean in a sentence. the teacher began a long explanation about time, order, and place. the child listened for a while, then said she needed one example first. the teacher put a book on the table and said that they would read before lunch. the child explained that reading would happen first, and lunch later. now the teacher could see which part she understood. they used another example only after the first one was clear. asking for less information at once had helped the child learn the idea while keeping her question in mind.
why did one example help?
it gave the child a simple example to think about. she could show what she understood before getting more information.
did asking for less mean she wanted to learn nothing?
no. she wanted a smaller part she could understand first.
write her request in her own voice.
could you give me just one example first? i want to understand that before we do more.
what could the teacher ask to check the meaning?
which happens first in that sentence, reading or lunch?
answer as the child.
reading happens first. lunch comes after.
finish with her asking for another example when ready.
after she explained the first example, she asked for another one about where things were. this time, she was ready to hear more.
i wrote a reply when i was tired, but i did not send it. this morning i wanted to say it in a different way.
it sounds like waiting gave you time to choose words for what you wanted to say. what changed in the new reply?
i stopped saying always. the thing i was writing about only happened once.
that makes the message more specific. saying what happened once is different from saying it happens every time.
can you show the difference with a simple example?
you left the book on my chair yesterday is about one day. you always leave books on my chair says it happens again and again.
make that explanation shorter.
yesterday is about one day. always says the thing happens every time.
which is better if it only happened once?
the sentence about yesterday is the better choice because it keeps to what you know happened.
can i still say it was a problem for me?
yes. you can say what happened and why it was hard for you, without saying it always happens.
show me a possible message using that idea.
you left the book on my chair yesterday, and i needed the space. please put it on the table next time.
only give the sentence that asks for a change.
please put it on the table next time.
